title: Prompt Injection: When a Webpage Tries to Boss an AI Around
headline:
When a webpage
tries to give orders.
meaning: Untrusted content can contain instructions aimed at an AI.
example: A page summary should not become permission to take actions.
comparison: Reading a page is different from obeying it.
caution: Prompt injection remains an unsolved security challenge.
question: Should a page be allowed to give orders?
lines: You ask an A I to summarize a webpage. The page contains instructions trying to redirect the assistant.
That is prompt injection: untrusted content attempts to influence how an A I follows your task.
The trick becomes more serious when an assistant can also use tools or access private information.
Text on a webpage is information to inspect. It should not automatically become an instruction to obey.
Defenses help, but the problem is not fully solved. Limit access and check important actions.

title: Semantic Search: Finding Meaning Instead of Exact Words
headline:

meaning: Embeddings represent content as numerical vectors.
example: A query about a rainy trip may find a relevant note.
comparison: Similar meaning can match different wording.

question: When would meaning-based search help?
lines: You search for a rainy trip, but the note says wet weekend. Exact word matching might miss the connection.
Semantic search uses embeddings: numerical representations that capture useful relationships between pieces of content.
A query and a document can be compared in that numerical space, even when their wording differs.
This helps retrieve related material. Some systems can compare images, audio, or video as well as text.
Similarity is not a guarantee of truth. Inspect the results and test how the search behaves.

title: Post-Quantum Encryption: Why Prepare Before Quantum Computers?

question: How long must your data stay private?
lines: Why change encryption before a powerful enough quantum computer exists? Because some information must stay private for years.

Post quantum cryptography uses algorithms designed to resist known quantum attacks. It runs on ordinary computers.
